name: Okta
description: Read Okta directory state: users, groups and assigned applications from an Okta org

tools.name: list_users
tools.description: List users in the Okta org (id, status, login, name, email, lifecycle timestamps)

limit.description: Users to return per page (default 25, max 200)

q.description: Optional prefix search across firstName, lastName and email

filter.description: Optional SCIM filter expression (e.g. status eq "ACTIVE")

after.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page's Link header

tools.name: get_user
tools.description: Get one Okta user by id or login: status, profile and lifecycle timestamps

user_id.description: Okta user id (e.g. 00u1abcdefGHIJ2klm3n4) or the user's login

tools.name: list_groups
tools.description: List Okta groups (id, name, description, type, object class, membership timestamps)

limit.description: Groups to return per page (default 25, max 200)

q.description: Optional prefix search on group name

filter.description: Optional SCIM filter expression (e.g. type eq "OKTA_GROUP")

after.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page's Link header

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: List applications configured in the Okta org (id, label, status, sign-on mode, visibility)

limit.description: Applications to return per page (default 20, max 200)

q.description: Optional prefix search on application name or label

filter.description: Optional SCIM filter expression (e.g. status eq "ACTIVE")

after.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous page's Link header

needs_review: READ-ONLY by design: no tool is marked write:true. Okta's user/group/app lifecycle operations (activate, suspend, deactivate, assign) are POSTs against the same token and are deliberately out of this wave.

base_url is tenant-prefixed. The vault field `domain` holds a bare host (registry placeholder 'dev-123456.okta.com'), so the template is https://{{domain}}. A customer who pastes 'https://dev-123456.okta.com' or a trailing path into that field would produce a malformed base URL; the field is not normalised anywhere today.

Okta orgs served on oktapreview.com (preview/sandbox) and custom vanity domains work through the same `domain` field, but the API token must be minted in the SAME org as the host: a mismatch surfaces as E0000011 'Invalid token provided', which is indistinguishable from a wrong token.

The shape-proof probes okta.okta.com (Okta's own production org) via base_url._probe. *.okta.com is wildcard-resolved, so a nonexistent tenant also answers the auth wall; the run proves the paths and the SSWS header shape against a live Okta API, not that any particular tenant exists.

Pagination is Link-header based (`after` cursor). The declarative response picker returns only the body, so an agent cannot page past the first `limit` results until the runtime surfaces response headers.
